title: Coffee Bean Pots de Crème
summary: Smooth baked custards with a deep coffee caramel flavour from cracked coffee beans, finished with whole beans.
equipment: food processor or rolling pin and bag
6 x 120 ml ramekins or small pots

ingredients.item: espresso-roast coffee beans, plus 12 to decorate

ingredients.note: plus a little extra to top up

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Crack the beans
steps.text: pulse the beans and cardamom a few times so they are roughly cracked, not ground. Cracked beans give flavour without making the cream gritty.

steps.title: Caramel
steps.text: stir the beans, cardamom and 100 g sugar in the pan over medium heat until the sugar melts and turns deep amber. Standing back, pour in 240 ml of the cream and the milk; it will spit and seize. Stir over the heat until smooth, bring to the boil, then cover off the heat and steep 20 min. Caramelising the sugar adds a toasty depth to the coffee.

steps.title: Custard
steps.text: heat the oven to 150 °C (130 °C fan). Whisk the yolks, 50 g sugar and salt until pale. Strain the coffee cream into the jug, pressing the beans, and add cream to make 480 ml. Whisk it slowly into the yolks without making froth.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: fill the ramekins in the tin, pour in hot water halfway up, cover with foil and bake about 40 min, until set with a slight wobble in the centre and 80 °C inside. Foil keeps a skin from forming and the heat gentle.

steps.title: Rest and chill
steps.text: leave in the water 10 min, then cool and chill at least 3 h. Serve near room temperature with 2 coffee beans on each.

tips: A common mistake is whisking hard, which makes bubbles on the custards; stir gently and skim any foam.
Leave out the cardamom for a pure coffee flavour.
The coffee beans on top are for decoration; most people set them aside.
storage: Cover and keep in the fridge for up to 2 days. Serve close to room temperature.
